I've reviewed the full implementation. Here is my assessment based strictly on the code and its behaviour.

The implementation is an Express + SQLite single-user bookmark app. Data model: `title, url, description, tags, favorite, created_at, updated_at`. Notably absent from the model: `note`, `unread`, `archived`, `snapshot`, and any page-metadata collection. It offers create/edit/delete, tag filtering, a simple LIKE search, and a "favorites" view (not "unread").

REF-BM-17/18/19: no unread flag or unread view; only a 'favorite' flag exists (not the same semantics). REF-BM-20: no multi-select or bulk actions. REF-BM-21: no filter-scoped bulk action. REF-BM-22: list order is hardcoded (favorite DESC, created_at DESC); no user-selectable sort key. REF-BM-23: no note field or markdown rendering. REF-BM-24/25: no local HTML/PDF snapshot or Internet Archive support. REF-BM-26/27/28: no archived flag; delete is the only removal. REF-BM-29: no bundles/saved filters. REF-BM-30/31: no Netscape HTML import/export. REF-BM-32: no user settings for sort/items-per-page/font size."
}
